utilities.tool.cron.phrase.label: Describe the schedule
utilities.tool.cron.phrase.assumption.ja: A yearly schedule needs a date; assumed January 1.
utilities.tool.cron.phrase.assumption.se: A fortnightly cadence has no single cron form; read as the 1st and the 15th.
utilities.tool.cron.phrase.assumption.da: Runs every day at that time
utilities.tool.cron.phrase.assumption.pm: Read the window end as {{shifted}}:00 ({{end}} pm)
utilities.tool.cron.phrase.caveat.domSte: The {{step}}-day step restarts at the start of every month, so the gap breaks at month boundaries (for example day 31 to day 1). For a strict every-{{step}}-days cadence, run daily and skip inside the job.
utilities.tool.cron.phrase.caveat.domDow: Cron treats day-of-month plus weekday as either/or: this fires on those dates AND on those weekdays, not only when both match.
utilities.tool.cron.phrase.caveat.nonsta: L (last day) is not POSIX-standard cron. Most modern schedulers accept it; check yours before relying on it.
utilities.tool.cron.phrase.caveat.noYear: Cron has no year field, so an every-{{step}}-years cadence cannot be expressed. This fires every January 1 instead.
utilities.tool.cron.phrase.caveat.nonsta: The # operator (nth weekday of the month) is a Quartz extension, not POSIX cron. Check your scheduler accepts it.
The L operator on a weekday (last one of the month) is a Quartz extension, not POSIX cron. Check your scheduler accepts it.
utilities.tool.cron.phrase.caveat.semiMo: The gap is not uniform: 14 days from the 1st to the 15th, then 14 to 17 days from the 15th to the next 1st.
utilities.tool.cron.phrase.unsupported.m: Cron cannot express a continuous every-{{step}}-weeks schedule — day steps restart each month. Closest options: fixed days like 1,15, or run weekly and skip inside the job.
One cron expression cannot combine times with different minutes: the fields multiply, so 8:15 and 20:30 would also fire at 8:30 and 20:15. Create one expression per time.
utilities.tool.cron.phrase.unrecognized: Could not turn that phrase into a schedule.
utilities.tool.cron.phrase.ai.hint: Uses the AI endpoint you configured. The answer only lands after the cron parser validates it.
utilities.tool.cron.phrase.ai.unconfigur: Add your AI endpoint, API key, and model in Settings → Account → AI to interpret free-form phrases.
utilities.tool.cron.phrase.ai.suggestion: Light local models handle this well — with Ollama try llama3.2:1b (~1.3 GB), qwen2.5:1.5b-instruct (~1 GB), or qwen2.5:0.5b-instruct (~0.4 GB): ollama pull llama3.2:1b
utilities.tool.cron.phrase.ai.upsell: AI assistance is a paid feature. Upgrade to interpret free-form phrases with your own AI endpoint.
utilities.tool.cron.phrase.ai.invalid: The model could not produce a valid cron expression for that phrase.
utilities.tool.cron.phrase.caveat.minute: 60 is not divisible by {{step}}, so this is not a continuous every-{{step}}-minutes cadence: the count restarts at the top of each hour, leaving a {{tail}}-minute gap before :00.
utilities.tool.cron.phrase.caveat.hourSt: 24 is not divisible by {{step}}, so this is not a continuous every-{{step}}-hours cadence: the count restarts at midnight, leaving a {{tail}}-hour gap before 00:00.
utilities.tool.cron.phrase.caveat.monthS: 12 is not divisible by {{step}}, so this is not a continuous every-{{step}}-months cadence: the count restarts each January, leaving a {{tail}}-month gap before it.
utilities.tool.cron.phrase.unsupported.s: A step of {{step}} does not fit this cron field (maximum {{max}}). Express it with the next larger unit instead — for example every 90 minutes is not representable, but every hour or every 2 hours is.
utilities.tool.cron.phrase.unsupported.c: The phrase asks for two competing cadences at once. Keep one interval per expression, or create one expression per cadence.
utilities.tool.cron.phrase.ai.retryNote: If the answer is not a valid 5-field expression, one corrective retry is sent containing this same phrase plus the validator rejection.
